People and organizations of the district.

organization · Carleton Place

Carleton Place Canoe Club

Canada's oldest continuously operating canoe club, founded in 1893 as the Ottawa Valley Canoe Association and reorganized under its present name in 1900. On the shores of the Mississippi River at Riverside Park, it has taught and raced paddlers of the district for over 130 years.

  • A charter member (1900) of the Canadian Canoe Association and the oldest club still in it; its first regatta ran at Lake Park in 1893.
  • Opened its membership to women in 1903 — among the first clubs anywhere to do so — and early ladies' war canoe championships were raced here.
  • A working origin of the town's paddling culture: sprint, high-performance, dragon boat and Paddle-ALL programs have produced numerous Canadian champions.
cpcanoeclub.com ↗
organization · Ashton · Carleton Place

Thomas Cavanagh Construction Limited

Eastern Ontario contractor and aggregates producer — construction, asphalt, concrete, land development and homebuilding — founded in 1953 by Thomas Cavanagh with a single dump truck. More than 1,200 employees across three divisions.

  • Head office on Highway 7 in Ashton since 1984; a concrete plant (Cavanagh Concrete) operates at 205 Industrial Avenue in Carleton Place.
  • Rebuilt the historic mill in Almonte as the Enerdu hydroelectric facility, completed 2018.
  • Founder's $1,000,000 gift to the Carleton Place & District Memorial Hospital named its emergency wing; the Thomas Cavanagh Foundation continues the giving.
